# CardBeat

> CardBeat is a digital corkboard for iPhone and iPad. Screenwriters and novelists plot a screenplay, novel or short story on index cards, one card per scene or beat, and can show the board on a TV or projector in a writers' room. It is free with two boards; a one-time in-app purchase unlocks unlimited boards. There is no subscription.

Key facts:

- Platforms: iPhone and iPad with iOS/iPadOS 26 or later, including iPhone Duo. There is no Mac, Windows, Android or web version.
- Price: free with two boards. CardBeat Pro is a one-time purchase that unlocks unlimited boards: $19.99 in the US, 19.99 € in the euro zone, prices vary by region.
- Cards: written by hand with Apple Pencil or a finger, or typed. Blank, lined, dotted or grid cards in eight colors. Cards can be placed anywhere, with optional snap-to-grid.
- Writers' room mode: on a connected TV, monitor or projector, CardBeat shows the board itself without toolbars, not a mirror of the iPad, and updates it live.
- Clean Up: lines cards up on an even grid without changing the order of acts and scenes.
- Sharing: export a board as a single-page PDF, or as a CardBeat file that a co-writer imports. There is no real-time collaboration on the same board.
- Sync: through the user's own iCloud account, and can be switched off.
- Privacy: no accounts, no ads, no third-party analytics. The app collects no data.
- Not a writing app: CardBeat is for structure. Writers draft the pages in apps such as Final Draft, Fade In, Highland or Scrivener.
- Made by Stefan Stuckmann, a TV showrunner, who built it for his own writers' room.
